Count the day of injury plus every calendar day through Tuesday
Count zero days because the employee returned for the next scheduled shift after Monday

questions.stem: At a privacy-case review, a supervisor proposes: "Count only Monday because it was the only scheduled workday missed". The underlying case is: An employee is injured late Friday and a physician states that the employee cannot work Saturday through Monday. The employee was not scheduled on the weekend and returns Tuesday. How should days away be counted? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Count the day of injury plus every calendar day through Tuesday
Count zero days because the employee returned for the next scheduled shift after Monday
Count only Monday because it was the only scheduled workday missed
Count each calendar day the employee was unable to work, including the weekend days
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Days away are counted as calendar days beginning after the day of injury or illness, regardless of whether the employee was scheduled to work.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Count the day of injury plus every calendar day through Tuesday' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling days away counting principle.
The proposed response 'Count zero days because the employee returned for the next scheduled shift after Monday' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling days away counting principle.
The proposed response 'Count only Monday because it was the only scheduled workday missed' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling days away counting principle.

questions.stem: At a post-incident recordability meeting, a supervisor proposes: "A days-away case because any medical restriction is treated as absence". options: A recordable restricted-work case because the employee cannot perform a routine job function
A days-away case because any medical restriction is treated as absence
A nonrecordable case because the employee worked the full number of hours
A first-aid-only case unless the restriction continues for more than seven days
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Restriction exists when an employee cannot perform one or more routine functions or cannot work the full day normally scheduled. Full attendance does not eliminate the restriction.

The proposed response 'A nonrecordable case because the employee worked the full number of hours' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling restricted work principle.
The proposed response 'A first-aid-only case unless the restriction continues for more than seven days' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling restricted work principle.

The proposed response 'Record every injury occurring on company property without considering an exception' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling work-relatedness exception principle.
